message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"20.1","text":"During the night, he rose, woke us, and sat down as usual. He said, “Ask me about whatever you wish.” Sophonias was the first to begin with him: “Since we desire to learn, explain to us how the account concerning the evil one truly stands.” Peter said, “I have indeed already made it clear through the discussion with Simon, but because the things concerning him were stated together with other points, the matter was not brought to light very clearly. For many points that seem equal in force to the truth give most people some knowledge of the truth itself. Therefore, if I now tell you what I had then told Simon among many points, do not suppose that you have been honored equally with him.” Sophonias said, “You speak rightly. For if you now separate it out for us from the many points stated then, you will make the actual truth clearer.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὁ περὶ πονηροῦ λόγος","chosen":"the account concerning the evil one","rationale":"The adjective is substantival and refers contextually to the personal evil ruler discussed in the following sections; the broader alternative “the account concerning evil” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"τῷ δὲ σὺν ἑτέροις κεφαλαίοις τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰρηκέναι","chosen":"because the things concerning him were stated together with other points","rationale":"The articular infinitive gives the reason the subject was not presented clearly, while κεφάλαια denotes principal points or topics."},{"source_quote":"μὴ οἰηθῆτε ἴσῃ αὐτῷ τιμῇ τετιμῆσθαι","chosen":"do not suppose that you have been honored equally with him","rationale":"The implied subject is the present hearers, and αὐτῷ most naturally refers to Simon. Taking αὐτῷ as referring to the truth or preceding material is less consistent with Sophonias’s reply."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ πολλῶν τῶν τότε εἰρημένων κεφαλαίων ἀφορίζεις","chosen":"separate it out for us from the many points stated then","rationale":"The unstated object is contextually the subject under discussion or its truth; ἀφορίζεις means to distinguish or set apart."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"20.2","text":"Peter said, “Hear, therefore, the truth about the ordering concerning the evil one. God defined two kingdoms and constituted two ages. He decided that the present world was to be given to the evil one because it is small and passes away quickly, but he promised to give the coming age to the good one, since it is great and eternal. He therefore made the human being self-determining, with the capacity to incline toward whatever actions he wishes. His body is three-part and has its origin from the female, for it has desire, anger, grief, and the things that follow these. The spirit—though itself not third in origin but three-part—has its origin from the male and is receptive to reasoning, knowledge, fear, and the things that follow these. Each of the two triads has one root, so that the human being is from two compounds, female and male. For this reason two ways were also set before him, that of law and that of lawlessness. Two kingdoms were also defined: one called the kingdom of the heavens, and the other the kingdom of those now reigning upon the earth. Moreover, two kings were appointed. One is appointed by law to reign over the present and temporary world, and he was blended so as to delight in the destruction of the wicked. The other, himself also being king of the age that is to come, loves every human nature. Unable in the present circumstances to have freedom to speak openly ..... as, while trying to conceal who he is, he counsels what is beneficial.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς περὶ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἁρμονίας","chosen":"the ordering concerning the evil one","rationale":"ἁρμονία can denote an arrangement, composition, or harmonious ordering. “Ordering” suits the ensuing account of paired ages, kingdoms, rulers, and elemental mixtures."},{"source_quote":"αὐτεξούσιον","chosen":"self-determining","rationale":"The term describes possessing authority over one’s own choices, not unlimited power."},{"source_quote":"οὐ τριτογενὲς ὄν, ἀλλὰ τριμερές","chosen":"not third in origin but three-part","rationale":"The contrast distinguishes being third-generated or third in derivation from having three parts. “Not third-born” is a more literal alternative."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ φυραμάτων δύο","chosen":"from two compounds","rationale":"φυράματα evokes kneaded masses or mixtures; “compounds” preserves the author’s composite anthropology."},{"source_quote":"νόμῳ βασιλεύειν χειροτονεῖται","chosen":"is appointed by law to reign","rationale":"χειροτονεῖται denotes selection or appointment, while νόμῳ presents the appointment and rule as lawful."},{"source_quote":"ἐπ’ ὀλέθρῳ πονηρῶν χαίρειν ἐκράθη","chosen":"was blended so as to delight in the destruction of the wicked","rationale":"The compositional force of ἐκράθη is retained because the following section explains the rulers through elemental blending. πονηρῶν may denote wicked people or, less probably here, evil things."},{"source_quote":"τὴν παρρησίαν ἔχειν","chosen":"to have freedom to speak openly","rationale":"παρρησία can mean boldness, freedom of speech, or openness. The following effort to remain concealed favors the sense of speaking or acting openly."},{"source_quote":"τίς ποτ’ ἔστι λανθάνειν πειρώμενος","chosen":"while trying to conceal who he is","rationale":"The indirect question is taken as the identity the king attempts to conceal. Alternatively, the words could describe him more generally as trying to escape notice."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐν τοῖς παροῦσι τὴν παρρησίαν ἔχειν οὐ δυνάμενος ..... ὧς","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly five dots. Its content is unavailable, no restoration has been supplied, and all five dots are retained in the English.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὧς, τίς ποτ’ ἔστι λανθάνειν πειρώμενος","issue":"The circumflexed ὧς is difficult in this construction and may be an accentual error for the conjunction ὡς. The translation adopts that contextually defensible comparison and discloses the proposed correction.","proposed_reading":"ὡς, τίς ποτ’ ἔστι λανθάνειν πειρώμενος","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.3","text":"“Of these two ..... compels the other, at God’s command. Each person has authority ........... by which to obey whichever of them he wishes, for the purpose of doing good or evil. If someone chooses to do good things, he becomes the possession of the good king who is to come. But if someone should do base things, he becomes an instrument of the present evil one. Through sin, the latter has received authority over him by a just judgment; and, wishing to do so even before the coming age, he delights in punishing him in the present life and, while gratifying his own desire, carries out God’s will. The other was created to delight in exercising authority over righteous people. When he finds a righteous person, he rejoices greatly, saving him with eternal life; and he too, as though gratifying himself, offers God the thanks for these things. Every unjust person may be saved after changing his mind, and every righteous man may incur punishment for a final sin. But these two rulers are God’s swift hands, desiring to act beforehand in accomplishing his will. That this is so is also stated in the law in the person of God: ‘I will kill and make alive; I will strike, and I too will heal.’ For he truly kills and gives life. He kills through the left hand, that is, through the evil one who was blended so as to delight in the affliction of the impious. But he saves and benefits through the right hand, that is, through the good one who was created to delight in benefiting and saving the righteous. These have their substances not from outside God, for there is no other first principle. Yet they were not brought forth by God as living beings, for then they would have shared his disposition. Nor did they arise accidentally, having come into being spontaneously contrary to his purpose, since then the greatest part of his power would have been abolished. Rather, the four primary elements were brought forth from God: hot and cold, wet and dry. Thus he is indeed the father of every substance ..... disposition being what comes after the blending; for when they were blended outside, choice was born as their offspring. At the end of the present world, therefore, the evil one, after serving God blamelessly, can, since he is not of a single substance, become good when recomposed away from persistence in evil. For even now he does nothing evil, although he is evil, since he has lawfully received authority to inflict suffering.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὥ αὐτῶν ᾧ βούλεται πείθεσθαι","chosen":"by which to obey whichever of them he wishes","rationale":"ὥ is taken as a dative relative whose antecedent may have stood in the preceding lacuna, while αὐτῶν ᾧ means “whichever of them.” The construction remains uncertain because of the lost wording."},{"source_quote":"κτῆμα","chosen":"possession","rationale":"The word denotes something acquired or owned and presents the person as belonging to the coming good king."},{"source_quote":"ὑπηρέτημα","chosen":"instrument","rationale":"The formation denotes something that serves or ministers. “Servant” is possible, but “instrument” preserves the contrast with κτῆμα."},{"source_quote":"μεταμεληθέντι","chosen":"after changing his mind","rationale":"The verb can denote regret, reconsideration, or a change of mind. The context entails departure from injustice, but the distinct Greek term is not homogenized with the author’s other turning terminology."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τελευταίας ἁμαρτίας","chosen":"for a final sin","rationale":"τελευταίας may describe one last sin or a sin committed at the end of life. The rendering preserves the singular while leaving the temporal nuance possible."},{"source_quote":"ταχεῖαι χεῖρές εἰσι θεοῦ","chosen":"are God’s swift hands","rationale":"The author’s bodily image is preserved rather than reduced to “agents.”"},{"source_quote":"προλαμβάνειν ἐπιθυμοῦσαι τὸ αὐτοῦ θέλημα ἐπιτελεῖν","chosen":"desiring to act beforehand in accomplishing his will","rationale":"προλαμβάνειν conveys anticipation or acting in advance; the rulers perform divine punishment or benefit before final judgment."},{"source_quote":"ὁμόδοξοι γὰρ αὐτῷ ἦσαν","chosen":"for then they would have shared his disposition","rationale":"ὁμόδοξοι means sharing the same opinion or disposition, not the same glory. The counterfactual force is supplied by the surrounding argument."},{"source_quote":"ἔξω γὰρ κραθεῖσιν αὐτοῖς","chosen":"for when they were blended outside","rationale":"ἔξω is retained without an invented object. It may mean outside God or externally to the original divine bringing-forth."},{"source_quote":"ἅτε δὴ οὐ μιᾶς οὐσίας ὢν τῆς πρὸς κακίαν μονῆς μετασυγκριθεὶς ἀγαθὸς γενέσθαι δύναται","chosen":"can, since he is not of a single substance, become good when recomposed away from persistence in evil","rationale":"The genitive τῆς πρὸς κακίαν μονῆς is taken with μετασυγκριθεὶς as separation from persistence in evil. Alternatively, it may characterize a hypothetical single substance fixed in evil."},{"source_quote":"νομίμως κακουχεῖν εἰληφὼς τὴν ἐξουσίαν","chosen":"since he has lawfully received authority to inflict suffering","rationale":"The claim is that his punitive action is authorized, preserving the author’s distinction between being evil and acting outside the assigned law."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τῶν δὲ δύο τούτων ..... τὸν ἕτερον ἐκβιάζεται, θεοῦ κελεύσαντος","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly five dots where the grammatical subject or other governing wording may have stood. No subject has been restored, and the five dots remain explicit in the English.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐξουσίαν ἔχει........... ὥ αὐτῶν ᾧ βούλεται πείθεσθαι","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly eleven dots, retained in the English. The surviving ὥ may be a dative relative whose antecedent was in the lost wording, though an error or incomplete construction is also possible; no missing content has been supplied.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ὅθεν δὴ καὶ πατὴρ τυγχάνει πάσης οὐσίας ..... οὔσης γνώμης τῆς μετὰ τὴν κρᾶσιν","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly five dots between the statement about God as father of every substance and the phrase about disposition. No connective or missing claim has been supplied, and all five dots remain explicit.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.4","text":"After Peter said these things, Micaiah, who was also one of the followers, asked, “From where, then, does human sinning come?” Peter said, “It comes from not knowing that, when judgment has taken place concerning the things they do wrongly, they are certain to be punished. Consequently, although they possess desire for the continuation of life—as I said on another occasion—they satisfy it indiscriminately, through the corruption of half-mature boys or through some other pandering sin. Because they do not know that they are judged, as I said before, their lack of fear drives them to satisfy desire unlawfully. Thus God is not evil, for he established desire well so that there might be continuation of life. Rather, they themselves are most impious, since they have used what is good in desire badly. The same reasoning may also be applied to anger: someone who uses it justly, as is permitted, acts piously, but one who goes beyond the proper measure and takes judgment upon himself acts impiously.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"κρί[σεως γε]νομένης","chosen":"when judgment has taken place","rationale":"The genitive absolute places punishment after judgment concerning the wrongful acts; the selected edition marks part of the expression with brackets."},{"source_quote":"διαδοχὴν βίου","chosen":"the continuation of life","rationale":"The expression refers to the succession or perpetuation of human life through generation."},{"source_quote":"ταύτην πληροφοροῦσιν ὡς ἔτυχεν","chosen":"they satisfy it indiscriminately","rationale":"πληροφοροῦσιν here means bringing desire to fulfillment, while ὡς ἔτυχεν means casually, haphazardly, or without proper distinction."},{"source_quote":"ἤμ[ιπεπείρων] παίδων","chosen":"half-mature boys","rationale":"The marked adjective portrays the boys as only partly mature, literally half-ripened. “Half-grown children” is also possible because παίδων need not specify male sex in every context."},{"source_quote":"ἄλλῃ τινὶ κολακευούσῃ ἁμαρτίᾳ","chosen":"through some other pandering sin","rationale":"The participle portrays the sin as flattering or pandering to desire; “enticing sin” is a possible alternative."},{"source_quote":"τῷ καλῷ τῆς ἐπιθυμίας χρησάμενοι κακῶς","chosen":"they have used what is good in desire badly","rationale":"The wording distinguishes desire’s good divinely assigned function from its wrongful human use."},{"source_quote":"ἑαυτῷ τὴν κρίσιν λαβὼν","chosen":"takes judgment upon himself","rationale":"The phrase denotes personally assuming the authority to judge or punish."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"κρί[σεως γε]νομένης","issue":"The selected edition places σεως γε in square brackets within the phrase. The translation follows the resulting printed reading while disclosing its editorially marked status.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"εἶ[πον]","issue":"The selected edition places πον in square brackets to complete the verb. The translation follows the bracketed reading “I said.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"[εἰς] διαδοχὴν βίου","issue":"The preposition εἰς is printed in square brackets. The translation follows the selected edition’s marked construction without claiming recovery of independently verified wording.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἤμ[ιπεπείρων] παίδων","issue":"Most of the adjective is printed in square brackets, and the resulting initial accent and breathing are unusual beside the expected form ἡμιπεπείρων. The contextual meaning “half-mature” is defensible, but the marked letters remain editorially uncertain.","proposed_reading":"ἡμιπεπείρων παίδων","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20.5","text":"Sophonias spoke again: “Your patience, my lord Peter, grants us boldness to ask you many questions for the sake of precision. Therefore, taking courage, we conduct the examination in every way. I remember, then, that yesterday, while Simon was engaged in inquiry with you, he said that if the evil one was generated from God, it follows that he shares the same substance as the one who brought him forth and ought to have been good, not evil. You answered that this does not necessarily follow, since many evil people are born from good people. In the same way, two individuals unlike each other were born from Adam, one of whom was evil and the other good. When Simon objected that you had used human examples, you answered that by this reasoning one should not accept that God begets either, for this too is a human example. But I, Sophonias, accept that God begets; I do not accept that he begets evil, even if good people among human beings beget evil ones. And do not suppose that I irrationally ascribe to God some things pertaining to human beings but not others, because I concede begetting to him but do not ascribe to him the begetting of what is unlike him. Human beings naturally beget sons whose dispositions are unlike their own for the following reason: because they are composed of four parts, their bodies change in different ways according to different alterations; and in a human body, as the distinctive quality of the alteration at each particular time increases or decreases, it disrupts the proportionate mixture. Because the compounds do not always remain the same, the seeds are secreted at different times with different mixtures, and dispositions, whether good or evil, follow them in accordance with the mixture at that time. But in God’s case no such thing can be conceived, for since he is unchangeable and always existent, wh...... he might wish to bring forth, it is altogether necessary that what is brought forth by him should likewise ...... in every respect in relation to the one who begot it—I mean both substance and disposition. But if anyone should wish to call even him changeable, I do not know how he can also call him immortal.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἡ μακροθυμία σου","chosen":"your patience","rationale":"μακροθυμία denotes forbearance or patience, here Peter’s willingness to endure extensive questioning."},{"source_quote":"παρρησίαν ἡμῖν χαρίζεται","chosen":"grants us boldness","rationale":"Here παρρησία is the confidence or freedom to question Peter openly."},{"source_quote":"ἀκολούθως τῆς αὐτῆς τῷ προβαλόντι τυγχάνει οὐσίας","chosen":"it follows that he shares the same substance as the one who brought him forth","rationale":"ἀκολούθως marks Simon’s inference, while προβαλόντι is rendered “brought him forth” without imposing the more technical term “emanated.”"},{"source_quote":"ἀνόμοιοί τινες ὄντες δύο ἐγεννήθησαν","chosen":"two individuals unlike each other were born","rationale":"The ensuing contrast between the evil and good sons favors mutual dissimilarity, though the phrase could instead mean that both differed from Adam in some respect."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἀνθρώποις διαφερόντων","chosen":"things pertaining to human beings","rationale":"The phrase concerns features found among or associated with humans. “Things in which human beings differ” is grammatically possible but fits the stated contrast less well."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὰς διαφόρους τροπὰς διαφόρως τρέπονται τὰ σώματα","chosen":"their bodies change in different ways according to different alterations","rationale":"The repeated wordplay between τροπάς and τρέπονται is represented with “alterations” and “change”; the changes may include seasonal or elemental variation."},{"source_quote":"τὸ τῆς τροπῆς ἴδιον","chosen":"the distinctive quality of the alteration","rationale":"The phrase denotes the quality or component proper to a particular bodily change, likely one of the elemental qualities."},{"source_quote":"τὰ σπέρματα ἄλλοτε ἄλλην ἔχοντα κρᾶσιν ἀποκρίνονται","chosen":"the seeds are secreted at different times with different mixtures","rationale":"ἀποκρίνονται has the physiological sense of being separated or secreted, while κρᾶσιν continues the author’s language of elemental mixture."},{"source_quote":"ἄτρεπτον","chosen":"unchangeable","rationale":"The adjective directly contrasts God with the changing bodily mixtures described immediately before it."},{"source_quote":"τήν τε οὐσίαν λέγω καὶ τὴν γνώμην","chosen":"I mean both substance and disposition","rationale":"γνώμη here denotes disposition, purpose, or cast of mind. “Opinion” is possible but too narrow for the contrast between good and evil offspring."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἄτρεπτον γὰρ καὶ ἀεὶ ὢν, ὅπ...... προβάλλειν βουληθείη","issue":"The selected edition preserves only the fragment ὅπ before a lacuna of exactly six dots. The English represents the incomplete fragment as “wh......” and does not complete it as “whatever,” “whenever,” or another conjecture.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τὸ προβαλλόμενον αὐτῷ ὡσαύτως ...... τὰ πάντα τῷ γεγεννηκότι","issue":"The selected edition prints a lacuna of exactly six dots where wording governing the comparison with the begetter is unavailable. The English retains all six dots and does not supply a verb such as “resemble.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"εἰ [δὲ θελήσ]ειέ τις","issue":"The selected edition prints δὲ θελήσ in square brackets, completing the conditional expression. The translation follows that marked reading without proposing additional text.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
